title: 431. Why a boring life is beautiful

sentences.en: This is an iHeart Podcast, Guaranteed Human.
sentences.zh: 这是一档iHeart播客，由人类真情呈现。

sentences.en: I've been really trying to prioritize my health in a realistic way this year, and something that has kept me really motivated is my WHOOP.
sentences.zh: 今年我一直在以一种切合实际的方式认真优先考虑我的健康，而让我保持高昂动力的一大秘诀就是我的WHOOP。

sentences.en: I am such a data person, which is why I love WHOOP, because I can genuinely see why my body feels differently depending on the day, why I'm running differently,
sentences.zh: 我是一个非常注重数据的人，这也是我热爱WHOOP的原因，因为我能真切地看出为什么我的身体在不同的日子里会有不同的感觉，为什么我跑步的状态会有所不同，

sentences.en: why I'm maybe less focused.
sentences.zh: 为什么我可能注意力不那么集中。

sentences.en: WHOOP effortlessly tracks my sleep, it tracks my strain, my recovery, my stress, and most importantly, my overall health.
sentences.zh: WHOOP能轻松追踪我的睡眠、体能消耗、恢复情况、压力水平，最重要的是，还有我的整体健康状况。

sentences.en: And it just gives me all that data and all those patterns so I can make better decisions, which includes knowing when to go easy and knowing when to go hard.
sentences.zh: 它为我提供所有这些数据和模式，以便我能做出更好的决策，包括知道什么时候该轻松一点，什么时候该全力以赴。

sentences.en: New members can try WHOOP with a 30-day free trial before committing to a membership.
sentences.zh: 新会员在决定订阅之前，可以先通过30天免费试用体验WHOOP。

sentences.en: That's join.whoop.com slash psychology for your free month of WHOOP.
sentences.zh: 访问 join.whoop.com 并在斜杠后输入 psychology，即可免费体验一个月的WHOOP。

sentences.zh: 来Love Honey史上最棒的黑色星期五寻找你的心动体验，还有精美礼品隐秘配送。

sentences.en: Enjoy up to 70% off.
sentences.zh: 享受高达7折优惠。

sentences.zh: 更高级的Love Honey黑色星期五？

sentences.zh: Visit lovehoney.com.au.

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: I'm Gemma Spake, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through the biggest changes, moments, and transitions of our 20s,
sentences.zh: 我是杰玛·斯派克，欢迎回到《你二十岁的心理学》，这是一档带你探讨二十岁人生中最大的改变、高光时刻与转折点的播客，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及这些经历对我们心理意味着什么。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目中。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本期播客。

sentences.en: It is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 非常高兴你能回来收听新的一期节目，当然，我们将在这里剖析二十岁的心理学。

sentences.en: Today, let me get on my soapbox for a second and say a boring life is a beautiful life.
sentences.zh: 今天，请容许我站在讲台上发表个观点：平淡的生活才是美好的生活。

sentences.en: It is my belief that every single day we face this wall of content that wants to convince you that what you are doing isn't enough.
sentences.zh: 我坚信，我们每天都在面对铺天盖地的内容，它们试图说服你：你现在做的事情还远远不够。

sentences.en: And if you were to listen to this, like, tidal wave of, like, videos and posts and whatnot, you would honestly believe that everybody has more motivation than you.
sentences.zh: 如果你去听信这种铺天盖地的视频、帖子之类的信息巨浪，你真的会以为所有人都比你更有动力。

sentences.en: Everybody has more friends than you.
sentences.zh: 所有人的朋友都比你多。

sentences.en: Everybody has more clothes, more money, more kind of, like, action going on in their life.
sentences.zh: 所有人都拥有更多衣服、更多金钱，生活里有更多热闹和精彩。

sentences.en: First of all, that's not true.
sentences.zh: 首先，这不是真的。

sentences.en: But second, being boring is a radical act.
sentences.zh: 但其次，过一种平淡的生活是一种激进的举动。

sentences.en: There is no one to impress.
sentences.zh: 你无需向任何人证明什么。

sentences.en: There is no one else's life that you want to copy because you like what you have.
sentences.zh: 你也不需要去复制别人的生活，因为你很喜欢自己目前拥有的这一切。

sentences.en: You have no idea how much agency that acceptance of what other people might not see as glamorous gives you.
sentences.zh: 你根本无法想象，这种接受别人或许并不觉得光鲜亮丽的生活，能赋予你多大的自主权。

sentences.en: I also think the tidal wave is shifting and more of us are realizing how truly freeing it is to slow down and just go smaller and slower.
sentences.zh: 我也认为这种浪潮正在转变，我们当中越来越多的人开始意识到，慢下来、把生活过得更小更慢是多么地真正解放天性。

sentences.en: It's a bit of, it's revolutionary.
sentences.zh: 这有点，这具有革命性。

sentences.en: It's psychologically revolutionary.
sentences.zh: 这是心理学意义上的革命。

sentences.en: For sure.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So what we're going to talk about today is the beauty of the boring routine, the boring rituals and why they're important
sentences.zh: 所以我们今天要讨论的是平淡日常的美好、单调仪式的意义，以及它们为什么重要，

sentences.en: and why they may open doors you didn't even realize were available or were there, especially in your 20s.
sentences.zh: 为什么它们可能会为你打开那些你甚至从未意识到存在过的大门，尤其是在你的二十岁。

sentences.en: I also want to talk about how to cope with feeling like maybe you're wasting your youth and why that's absolutely not true.
sentences.zh: 我还想谈谈如何应对那种觉得自己可能在虚度青春的感觉，以及为什么这种想法绝对是无稽之谈。

sentences.en: Let's talk about it.
sentences.zh: 我们来聊聊这个。

sentences.en: Why is the boring life beautiful?
sentences.zh: 为什么平淡的生活是美好的？

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: So what do I mean when I say a boring life?
sentences.zh: 那么，当我提到平淡的生活时，究竟是什么意思？

sentences.en: Because I feel like that's kind of open to interpretation.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得这个概念有点开放性，可以有不同的解读。

sentences.en: For me, and it may be different for you, a boring life is just one that I think has maybe been dismissed by social media because it's not as easy to sell into.
sentences.zh: 对我而言——对你来说可能有所不同——平淡的生活只是一种我认为可能被社交媒体所贬低的生活方式，因为它不容易被用来带货。

sentences.en: It is the one where you don't buy new clothes every week because that's ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种你不会每周都买新衣服的生活，因为那太荒谬了。

sentences.en: You don't need to go on lavish vacations every month to be happy because who can afford that?
sentences.zh: 你不需要为了快乐而每个月都去奢华度假，因为谁能承担得起那样的开销呢？

sentences.en: You don't need to be constantly engaged in drama or emotional extremes just to feel stimulated.
sentences.zh: 你不需要时刻卷入戏剧冲突或情绪极端中，仅仅为了寻求刺激。

sentences.en: But instead, you have firm boundaries.
sentences.zh: 相反，你有坚定的边界。

sentences.en: You have a routine you like.
sentences.zh: 你有自己喜欢的日常作息。

sentences.en: You have small luxuries.
sentences.zh: 你有微小的奢侈。

sentences.en: You have stability, tiny joys, peace really.
sentences.zh: 你有稳定性、小小的快乐，以及真正的平静。

sentences.en: When I kind of picture it for myself, it's very grammar coded.
sentences.zh: 当我在脑海中为自己描绘这种画面时，它非常具有“奶奶风”的代码感。

sentences.en: Maybe I'd use the term like slow maxing if I was that kind of person.
sentences.zh: 如果我是那种人的话，我可能会用“低配慢活”这样的词。

sentences.en: But like, again, indulgence in simple pleasures, appreciation for what you have now without constantly desiring more, slowing down, simplicity.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，就是沉浸在简单的快乐中，对你现在拥有的东西心存感激，而不是一味地渴望更多，放慢节奏，回归简单。

sentences.en: And from the outside, yes, something that might look really boring or maybe lame, but when we get down to it is deeply nourishing
sentences.zh: 从外表来看，是的，这种生活可能看起来真的很枯燥甚至有点无趣，但当我们深入其中时，它会带来极大的滋养，

sentences.en: and supremely fulfilling for our psychological needs.
sentences.zh: 并且极大地满足我们的心理需求。

sentences.en: I don't think I'm the only one seeing this like mass conversion, mass trend back to this kind of simple, understated existence.
sentences.zh: 我想我不是唯一一个看到这种大规模回归、大规模转回这种简单、低调生存状态的人。

sentences.en: We've noticed it in like the trend of the trad wife, but also just like in my friends and in myself included, this craving for a life that's more manageable.
sentences.zh: 我们在诸如“传统妻子”这种潮流中注意到了这一点，而且在我的朋友们以及我自己身上也能感受到这种对更可控生活的渴望。

sentences.en: When previously, you know, we really kind of ran on fumes and kind of had these very packed schedules and we thought that was success.
sentences.zh: 而在此之前，你知道的，我们真的是在透支精力，日程排得满满当当，并且还认为那就是成功。

sentences.en: Part of this is developmental.
sentences.zh: 这种现象的一部分是由于身心发育成熟。

sentences.en: As we get older, even within our 20s, which is, by the way, still very young, many people become, we just become less drawn to raw stimulation for its own sake.
sentences.zh: 随着我们年龄的增长，甚至在二十多岁这个顺便说一句依然非常年轻的阶段，许多人对纯粹为了刺激而追求刺激的兴趣都在减弱。

sentences.en: There was a very interesting study done in 2014 that looked at, I think data from like almost 6,000 individuals,
sentences.zh: 2014年曾有过一项非常有趣的研究，我记得它分析了近6000名个体的数据，

sentences.en: and they measured changes in impulsivity and sensation-seeking behaviours from the ages of 15 to 26.
sentences.zh: 他们测量了15岁至26岁之间冲动性和寻求刺激行为的变化。

sentences.en: And what they noticed was that, obviously, as we get older, those impulses reduce.
sentences.zh: 他们注意到的是，很显然，随着我们年龄的增长，这些冲动会减少。

sentences.en: But it specifically found that this drive towards the karma, boring life in our 20s is being driven by two things.
sentences.zh: 但研究具体发现，我们在二十多岁时对平静、平淡生活的这种向往，是由两件事驱动的。

sentences.en: Firstly, changes in our personality.
sentences.zh: 首先是人格的变化。

sentences.en: And secondly, a linear decline in impulsivity and in risk-taking behaviour and hunger for novelty.
sentences.zh: 其次是冲动性、冒险行为以及对新鲜事物渴望的线性下降。

sentences.en: We kind of know what we want.
sentences.zh: 我们渐渐知道了自己想要什么。

sentences.en: We don't need raw excitement to motivate us.
sentences.zh: 我们不再需要强烈的刺激来激励自己。

sentences.en: Like we have the pull and the drive of long-term gratification and long-term peace and long-term stability
sentences.zh: 就像长远满足感、长远平静以及长远稳定对我们的吸引力和驱动力，

sentences.en: is more motivational and more convincing.
sentences.zh: 变得更具激励作用和说服力。

sentences.en: Another part of this and why we notice this change is that in reality, like chaos eventually costs you too much and it loses its attraction as we get older.
sentences.zh: 其中的另一个原因，也是我们注意到这种变化的原因在于，现实中混乱终究会让你付出太大的代价，随着我们年龄的增长，它会失去吸引力。

sentences.en: When you're younger or like when you're still kind of constructing a sense of self,
sentences.zh: 当你更年轻的时候，或者当你还在构建自我意识的时候，

sentences.en: unpredictability, spontaneity, the pursuit of more,
sentences.zh: 不可预测性、自发性、对更多的追求，

sentences.en: I think that feels like proof that you are open and you're alive and you're an interesting person.
sentences.zh: 我 N 觉得这就像是证明你思想开放、充满活力且是一个有趣的人的证据。

sentences.en: It's like also almost like proof that, you know, I'm young, look at it, like look at this, I'm doing all these things.
sentences.zh: 这也几乎就像是在证明，你知道的，“我很年轻，看啊，看看我，我正在做所有这些事情。”

sentences.en: But over time, I think we do begin to notice how being constantly overwhelmed and stimulated is not necessarily the same thing as being fulfilled.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间推移，我想我们确实开始注意到， constantemente 感到不知所措和受到刺激，并不一定等于内心充实。

sentences.en: And we also see the burnout that happens when we have plans every single night, when we are kind of living on just like the fumes and highs of life.
sentences.zh: 而且我们也能看到，当每个晚上都有安排、当我们在生活中仅仅靠着精疲力竭和亢奋勉强维系时，所带来的职业倦怠。

sentences.en: It's not that we don't crave less life, we just crave less friction and we learn what we don't like about the chaos.
sentences.zh: 并不是说我们不再渴望生活，我们只是渴望更少的摩擦，并且我们懂得了我们不喜欢混乱的哪些方面。

sentences.en: Why does it feel weird to admit that though?
sentences.zh: 然而，为什么承认这一点感觉怪怪的呢？

sentences.en: Like why does it feel weird to admit that we seemingly want less, not less per se but different?
sentences.zh: 为什么承认我们似乎想要更少——不是真正意义上的更少，而是不同——感觉很奇怪？

sentences.en: I think right before you are like able to fully accept like, hey, actually, I don't care what other people say, I want this boring life, we have this thing,
sentences.zh: 我想就在你能够完全接受诸如“嘿，事实上，我不在乎别人怎么说，我就想要这种平淡的生活”之前，我们会经历这样一种东西，

sentences.en: this kind of reaction that we actually call in psychology reactance, which is when it feels like our freedom to be young is being taken away,
sentences.zh: 这种我们在心理学上称之为“抗拒”的反应，也就是当感觉我们保持年轻的自由被剥夺时，

sentences.en: even if it's by our own choices, we kind of act out as like a last hurrah.
sentences.zh: 哪怕这是我们自己的选择，我们也会像进行最后狂欢一样做出反叛的举动。

sentences.en: What it's really coming down to is cognitive dissonance between what we're deeply craving internally and what the world around us has told us to desire and expect externally
sentences.zh: 归根结底，这是内心深处真正渴望的东西与周围世界告知我们在外部应当渴望和期待的东西之间产生的认知失调，

sentences.en: that feels like we're trapped between these two ways of living.
sentences.zh: 这让人感觉自己被困在了这两种生活方式之间。

sentences.en: There is this narrative that our 20s are supposed to be this incredibly fast-paced, hustle-filled, thousand plans a weekend kind of life before like so-called real life begins.
sentences.zh: 有一种说法认为，我们的二十岁就应该是那种节奏极快、充满内卷、每周末都有上千个安排的生活，仿佛真正的生活才刚刚开始一样。

sentences.en: You know, you're meant to kind of front load the stress and socializing of life as an investment for later on.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你注定要把人生的压力和社交在前几年做足，以此作为对未来的投资。

sentences.en: And yeah, at certain times in your life, it's really fun to do that.
sentences.zh: 是的，在人生的某些特定阶段，这样做确实很有趣。

sentences.en: And there's definitely seasons for it.
sentences.zh: 而且这绝对有它对应的时期。

sentences.en: But I don't like the idea that you have to keep doing things and keep forcing yourself into like busy chaos, even if you don't like it, just because that's the norm.
sentences.zh: 但我不喜欢这种观念：仅仅因为那是常态，你就必须不停地做事，强迫自己陷入繁忙的混乱中，哪怕你并不喜欢。

sentences.en: That gap between what we think we should want and what we genuinely do creates a lot of inattention.
sentences.zh: 我们认为自己应该想要的东西与我们内心真正想要的东西之间的差距，会产生大量的注意力不集中。

sentences.en: If the version of youth we've been convinced into is marketed as kind of constant excitement, then choosing calm can feel kind of unfairly, like you are failing at being young.
sentences.zh: 如果我们被灌输的青春版本被营销成了一种持续不断的兴奋状态，那么选择平静就会让人觉得有一种不公平的感觉，仿佛你正在把年轻过得很失败。

sentences.en: You know, am I wasting this decade?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，“我是不是在浪费这十年？”

sentences.en: Am I becoming, am I slowing down too soon?
sentences.zh: “我是不是老得太快了？”

sentences.en: Am I going to regret this?
sentences.zh: “我以后会后悔吗？”

sentences.en: Shocker.
sentences.zh: 真是令人震惊。

sentences.en: But that's basically yet another yardstick, which we're encouraged to use as a measure of apparent success of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 但这基本上是又一个衡量标准，我们被鼓励用它来评判自己二十岁是否取得了表面上的成功。

sentences.en: It's another thing that we're meant to judge ourselves by and always feel like we're not doing well enough because of.
sentences.zh: 这是我们用来审视自己的又一个标杆，并且因此总是觉得自己做得还不够好。

sentences.en: It's also not quite a shocker that since the introduction of social media, this sense of dissonance has increased.
sentences.zh: 毫不意外的是，自从社交媒体出现以来，这种失调感便加剧了。

sentences.en: At a level, researchers and social scientists actually can't quite measure fast enough.
sentences.zh: 其程度甚至让研究人员和社会科学家都无法足够快地进行测量。

sentences.en: One University of Washington study actually talks about how social media especially creates a state of firstly, reduced self-reflection, secondly, narrowed attention,
sentences.zh: 华盛顿大学的一项研究实际上探讨了社交媒体是如何导致首先自我反思减少、其次注意力狭隘、

sentences.en: and thirdly, lack of individual interest, all of which is correlated with greater unhappiness.
sentences.zh: 以及第三缺乏个人兴趣的，所有这些都与更高的不幸福感息息相关。

sentences.en: What these studies and what these findings basically say is that we get so focused on how others are living that the result of that is that we can no longer properly articulate
sentences.zh: 这些研究和发现基本上说明了，我们过于关注别人的生活，其结果就是我们再也无法清晰地表达

sentences.en: or even imagine what we actually want because we're so consumed with what apparently is making them happy.
sentences.zh: 甚至想象自己真正想要什么，因为我们被那些显然带给别人快乐的东西吞噬了。

sentences.en: I read this fantastic sub-stack the other day that was like, the loneliest place in the world is your full you page.
sentences.zh: 前几天我读到了一篇非常精彩的Substack文章，里面提到：“世界上最孤独的地方就是你的‘为你推荐’页面。”

sentences.en: And this author talks about like the masochism of the scroll where we kind of torture ourselves with the lives of people
sentences.zh: 这位作者谈到了刷屏的自虐心理，我们通过看那些人的生活来折磨自己，

sentences.en: that we don't really want to be like but convince ourselves we do and kind of torture ourselves by not being like.
sentences.zh: 虽然我们并不真的想成为那样的人，却说服自己想要成为，并且因为自己不像他们而备受折磨。

sentences.en: This gets to like a very vital point.
sentences.zh: 这就触及了一个至关重要的点。

sentences.en: What our equal fear but also desire for the boring life is really being manipulated by is FOMO.
sentences.zh: 我们对平淡生活的恐惧与渴望实际上正在被“FOMO（错失恐惧症）”所操控。

sentences.en: Like that's really what it is.
sentences.zh: 没错，事实就是这样。

sentences.en: Your failure or your inability to accept that this is what you actually want really comes down to this fear of missing out.
sentences.zh: 你之所以失败或无法接受这就是你真正想要的生活，归根结底还是因为这种错失恐惧。

sentences.en: Psychologists in a now very famous 2021 study defined the fear of missing out as a persistent apprehension that other people might be having more rewarding experiences without us
sentences.zh: 如今在2021年一项非常著名的研究中，心理学家将错失恐惧症定义为一种挥之不去的忧虑，即别人可能会在没有我们的参与下获得更多有益的体验，

sentences.en: paired with the urge to stay continually connected to what everyone else is doing.
sentences.zh: 并伴随着一种持续与其他人正在做的事情保持连接的冲动。

sentences.en: It is a social fear and therefore quite an existential fear striking at our core need to kind of not be alone in the experience or not be alone in the world.
sentences.zh: 这是一种社会恐惧，因此也是一种相当的存在主义恐惧，它直接击中了我们内心深处的需要——即在经历中不孤单，或在世界上不孤单。

sentences.en: That is why we feel like we're missing out by choosing what is not the norm.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么当我们选择不走寻常路时，会觉得自己错过了什么。

sentences.en: What is so interesting about this feeling is that it doesn't actually need evidence or need you to feel especially unhappy with your current situation to occur.
sentences.zh: 这种感觉最有趣的地方在于，它的产生并不需要证据，也不需要你对现状感到特别不快乐。

sentences.en: I think we often think of FOMO as like that's what happens to people who are very lonely, in their bedroom, visibly isolated
sentences.zh: 我想我们经常认为错失恐惧症只会发生在那些非常孤独、待在自己卧室里、肉眼可见地被孤立的人身上，

sentences.en: but we can be in the middle of like a movie night at home, best friend on the left, other friend to the right,
sentences.zh: 但我们完全可能正身处家中看电影的温馨氛围中，左边是最好的朋友，右边是另一个朋友，

sentences.en: staring at an Instagram story and suddenly feeling this pain and anxiety that even though we are happy in this moment,
sentences.zh: 却盯着Instagram的故事，突然感到一种痛苦和焦虑：尽管我们此刻很开心，

sentences.en: somebody else, somewhere else is having more fun and that's where we should be.
sentences.zh: 但在别处的某个地方，有人正在享受更多乐趣，而那才应该是我们所在的地方。

sentences.en: Somebody else is more alive than we are and therefore we are doing this wrong.
sentences.zh: 别人比我们活得更精彩，因此我们把生活过错了。

sentences.en: Like our quiet life is costing us this like more exciting level or more exciting version of youth.
sentences.zh: 仿佛我们的平静生活让我们付出了代价，错失了这种更刺激的层面或更刺激的青春版本。

sentences.en: FOMO is evolutionary in origin, we can't forget that.
sentences.zh: 从起源来看，FOMO具有演化上的根源，我们不能忘记这一点。

sentences.en: It's meant to drive us back to the herd but all it does in these moments is create this overwhelming sense of inadequacy.
sentences.zh: 它的本意是驱使我们回归群体，但在这些时刻，它所做的一切只是制造出一种势不可挡的不胜任感。

sentences.en: Instead of letting life unfold according to what we actually want and what feels good, it keeps us mentally oriented towards the road not taken.
sentences.zh: 它没有让生活根据我们真正想要和感觉舒适的方式自然展开，而是让我们在精神上始终关注着那条未曾走过的路。

sentences.en: It keeps us focused on the party we didn't go to, the trip we weren't invited on, the people we didn't meet by not going on that trip,
sentences.zh: 它让我们一直惦记着那个我们没去的派对、那个没邀请我们的旅行、那个因为没有去旅行而没有遇到的人，

sentences.en: the version of ourselves we imagine might have been if we had just said yes more often, stayed out later, been more tired, bought that item,
sentences.zh: 如果我们当初更经常地对各种事情说“好”、在外面待得更晚、更疲惫、买下那个东西，我们想象中自己本可以成为的那个版本，

sentences.en: even if in the moment we didn't want that.
sentences.zh: 即使当时我们并不想要那些。

sentences.en: A 2013 study published in the journal, I think it's like human behavior, conducted a series of studies looking at the concept of FOMO in relation to various factors
sentences.zh: 发表在《人类行为》杂志上的一项2013年的研究，开展了一系列研究，探讨了FOMO概念与人口统计、动机、幸福感等各种因素的关系，

sentences.en: like demographics, motivation, well-being, as well as how FOMO relates to behavior and emotional well-being.
sentences.zh: 以及FOMO如何与行为和情感福祉相关联。

sentences.en: What they found was that not only was FOMO linked to lower mood, lower overall life satisfaction, but also greater distraction from our own lives.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，FOMO不仅与情绪低落、整体生活满意度降低有关，还与对我们自己生活的更多分心有关。

sentences.en: People who were experiencing greater FOMO actually had poor autobiographical memory because they were so consumed with comparison they couldn't appreciate the moment they were in,
sentences.zh: 体验到更严重FOMO的人实际上自传体记忆更差，因为他们太沉迷于比较，以至于无法欣赏自己身处的当下，

sentences.en: good or bad.
sentences.zh: 无论是好是坏。

sentences.en: The really painful part is that FOMO can make us mistrust our own preferences.
sentences.zh: 真正痛苦的是，FOMO会让我们对自己的喜好产生不信任。

sentences.en: Like I've said this whole time, a boring life is beautiful if you can trust in its beauty and in your desire for it.
sentences.zh: 正如我一直所说，如果你能相信它的美好以及你对它的渴望，平淡的生活就是美好的。

sentences.en: But if you can't because you are constantly flooded with how other people are living, it's not going to feel as enjoyable.
sentences.zh: 但如果你因为不断被别人的生活狂轰滥炸而无法相信，它就不会让人觉得那么享受了。

sentences.en: The other reason I think we may feel apprehension of the boring life is because we think that boring, slow, peaceful, regulated means no more fun, no more excitement.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们可能会对平淡生活感到忧虑的另一个原因，是因为我们认为平淡、缓慢、平静、规律意味着不再有乐趣、不再有刺激。

sentences.en: Especially the kind of excitement we might find in like a messy night out or like bad decisions or drama.
sentences.zh: 尤其是那种我们在混乱的夜晚出行或糟糕的决定和戏剧性事件中可能会找到的刺激。

sentences.en: Again, I think there is a time and a place for that.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我认为这有它的时间和地点。

sentences.en: As much as I have,
sentences.zh: 尽管我有过这样的经历——

sentences.en: I've had moments like that, I regret moments like that.
sentences.zh: 我有过那样的时刻，我也为那样的时刻感到后悔。

sentences.en: I also cherish them equally because they are fundamental to who I am.
sentences.zh: 但我也同样珍视它们，因为它们是我之所以成为现在的我的基础。

sentences.en: But I don't need to learn those lessons again.
sentences.zh: 但我不需要再去吸取那些教训了。

sentences.en: And I don't need to learn those lessons again and again and again.
sentences.zh: 我不需要一遍又一遍、没完没了地去吸取同样的教训。

sentences.en: Like I'm done.
sentences.zh: 就像，我受够了。

sentences.en: And what was the lesson for if not kind of showing me how to make better decisions?
sentences.zh: 如果这些教训不是为了教会我如何做出更好的决定，那它们又是为了什么呢？

sentences.en: On a neurological level, like yeah, our brains do crave novelty but that's not novelty if you've already been in that situation and know you don't like it.
sentences.zh: 在神经科学的层面，是的，我们的大脑确实渴望新鲜感，但如果你已经经历过那种情况并且知道自己不喜欢它，那就不能算新鲜感了。

sentences.en: We are definitely, you know, wired to move towards what is surprising and unpredictable because novelty recruits so many different brain systems involved in attention
sentences.zh: 我们绝对是，你知道的，生来就被驱动去寻找令人惊讶和不可预测的事物，因为新鲜感会调动许多涉及注意力的大脑系统

sentences.en: and motivation and reward.
sentences.zh: 以及动机和奖励机制。

sentences.en: It's a huge factor in how our brain releases dopamine, right?
sentences.zh: 这是我们的大脑如何释放多巴胺的一个巨大因素，对吧？

sentences.en: Because we're always wanting to move towards what feels unfamiliar to learn and because of the anticipation and because of the possibility of pleasure.
sentences.zh: 因为我们总是想要去接近那些感觉陌生、可以学习的事物，出于期待，也出于对快乐的可能性的追求。

sentences.en: But we have to understand just because dopamine is powerful, just because our motivational systems are powerful doesn't mean they're always leading us in the right direction.
sentences.zh: 但我们必须明白，仅仅因为多巴胺很强大，仅仅因为我们的动机系统很强大，并不意味着它们总是在引导我们走向正确的方向。

sentences.en: But where we often get lost is in how we interpret that need for novelty and the feel-good of this dopamine.
sentences.zh: 但我们经常迷失的地方，在于我们如何解读对新鲜感的这种需求，以及多巴胺带来的这种好感觉。

sentences.en: Even though they feel similar at first, novelty isn't the same
sentences.zh: 尽管它们一开始感觉很相似，但新鲜感并不等同于

sentences.en: as pure chaos or the kind of busy lives that we think we need, right?
sentences.zh: 纯粹的混乱，或者那种我们以为自己需要的大忙人生活，对吧？

sentences.en: There are different levels of how dopamine is produced and received.
sentences.zh: 多巴胺的分泌和接收有不同的层级。

sentences.en: What we really need to understand is that the dopamine or whatever pleasure chemicals you were previously getting from this chaotic life that maybe you loved
sentences.zh: 我们真正需要理解的是，你之前从这种也许你曾经热爱

sentences.en: and that you were living is not the same that you're going to get from long-term gratification.
sentences.zh: 且正在经历的混乱生活中获得的多巴胺，或是任何快乐化学物质，与你从长期满足感中获得的是不一样的。

sentences.en: Sometimes we mistake the emotional highs and lows of chaos for evidence that we're really living, like how somebody in their 20s should be living.
sentences.zh: 有时候，我们会把混乱带来的情绪高潮和低谷误认为是真正生活的证明，就像二十多岁的人该过的生活那样。

sentences.en: But that immediate feeling of stimulation rarely gives us the deeper reward that true novelty and curiosity and enjoyment does.
sentences.zh: 但那种即时的刺激感很少能带给我们像真正的新鲜感、好奇心和享受所带来的那种更深层的回报。

sentences.en: In fact, one 2016 study from the neurology department at the University College of London actually found that it can actually create biased choices, like our striving
sentences.zh: 事实上，伦敦大学学院神经病学系2000年的研究发现，它确实会产生有偏差的选择，比如我们对

sentences.en: for quick dopamine, for instant pleasure,
sentences.zh: 追求快速多巴胺、即时快乐的渴望，

sentences.en: yes, may give us a faster result, but it creates an emotional crash later on.
sentences.zh: 是的，可能会给我们带来更快的结果，但它随后会造成情绪崩溃。

sentences.en: You know, we're constantly activated.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们总是处于被激活的状态。

sentences.en: We're not necessarily enriched.
sentences.zh: 我们未必得到了充实。

sentences.en: And again, this is the beauty of the boring life.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这就是平淡生活的魅力所在。

sentences.en: It takes you out of this constant state of needing more, of expectance, of anticipation, and allows you to just actually choose where your body and your mind wants to flow to
sentences.zh: 它让你从这种不断需要更多、充满期待和预期的状态中抽离出来，让你能够真正选择你的身体和心灵想要流向哪里，

sentences.en: and where you actually want to put your attention towards.
sentences.zh: 以及你真正想把注意力放在哪里。

sentences.en: Like, real novelty, real dopamine expands and enriches you.
sentences.zh: 就像真正的新鲜感和真正多巴胺会扩展并充实你一样。

sentences.en: It's in learning something new.
sentences.zh: 它在于学习新东西。

sentences.en: It's in deepening intimacy with friends or your partner.
sentences.zh: 它在于加深与朋友或伴侣的亲密关系。

sentences.en: it's getting into nature.
sentences.zh: 它在于融入大自然。

sentences.en: It's dedication to long-term projects or challenges.
sentences.zh: 它在于投身长期的项目或挑战。

sentences.en: I think that's what a boring life allows you to do.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是平淡生活能让你做到的事情。

sentences.en: Okay, let's take a short break here before we talk about what leaning into the intentionality and acceptance of a boring, lame life can do for you psychologically in terms of
sentences.zh: 好了，在我们探讨倾心于平淡、无趣生活的笃定与接纳能在心理上为你带来什么之前，我们先在这里休息一下，谈谈它在

sentences.en: your relationships and emotionally and why it's so good for you.
sentences.zh: 人际关系和情绪上为什么对你这么好。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: I've been approaching my health really differently this year.
sentences.zh: 今年我对健康的看法真的有了很大的改变。

sentences.en: I used to be really focused on maximizing and doing more and now I'm just realizing that if I listen to what my body needs I perform way better and that's why I am obsessed
sentences.zh: 我以前真的很专注于追求极致和做更多的事，现在我只是意识到，如果我倾听身体的需求，我的表现就会好得多，这就是为什么我痴迷于

sentences.en: with my WHOOP.
sentences.zh: 我的WHOOP。

sentences.en: Truly you guys, you know I'm such a data and information driven person and I love opening my WHOOP app and seeing how my sleep, my stress, my strain is correlating with my mood,
sentences.zh: 真的，大家伙儿，你们知道我是个极其注重数据和信息的人，我喜欢打开WHOOP应用，看看我的睡眠、压力、消耗是如何与我的心情、

sentences.en: with my running performance, with how I'm just feeling day to day.
sentences.zh: 我的跑步表现以及我每天的日常感受相关联的。

sentences.en: I'm not an elite athlete by any means but I do really benefit and I also just really enjoy knowing more about my body and WHOOP also gives me these actionable personalized insights
sentences.zh: 我绝不是什么顶尖运动员，但我确实受益匪浅，而且我也真的很喜欢多了解自己的身体，WHOOP还为我提供这些可操作的个性化见解，

sentences.en: that have made me more intentional and meant that I make smarter decisions day to day about what I need rather than just putting my foot on the gas and just going, going, going,
sentences.zh: 这些见解让我变得更有意识，这意味着我每天能针对自己的需求做出更明智的决定，而不是只知道踩着油门一味地往前冲、往前冲、往前冲、

sentences.en: going.
sentences.zh: 冲。

sentences.en: In order to convince you even more of the beauty in your so-called boring life that social media has convinced you to hate, let's talk about the four major changes and benefits you
sentences.zh: 为了让你更加确信社交媒体让你厌恶的那种所谓平淡生活的美好，让我们来谈谈当你接受慢节奏时会看到的四大重大改变和好处。

sentences.en: will see when you accept a slower pace.
sentences.zh: 第一，看似安静的生活，往往是情绪调节能力更好、极端低谷更少的生活。

sentences.en: Number one, what looks like a quieter life is often a life with better emotional regulation and fewer extreme lows.
sentences.zh: 当我们的生活过度受刺激时，大脑就会花更多时间处于过度唤醒状态。

sentences.en: When our lives become overstimulated, our brains spend more time in the state of hyperarousal.
sentences.zh: 皮质醇、肾上腺素保持升高，精神变得支离破碎，我们开始从反应性的角度而不是有意图的角度来行事。

sentences.en: Cortisol, adrenaline, they stay elevated, tension becomes fragmented, and we begin operating from a place of reactivity rather than intentionality.
sentences.zh: 关于压力的研究、关于神经系统调节的研究一再表明，长期的过度刺激会降低我们控制情绪的能力，正如我们之前提到的，

sentences.en: Research on stress, research on nervous system regulation consistently shows that chronic overstimulation reduces our capacity for emotional control and, as we mentioned before,
sentences.zh: 会降低我们做出基于良好价值判断的决策的能力。

sentences.en: reduces our capacity to make good value-based decisions.
sentences.zh: 我们对小麻烦、小挫折在情绪上变得更加脆弱，因为我们的基准压力已经很高了，稍微一点事就能把我们压垮。

sentences.en: We become more emotionally vulnerable to small inconveniences, to small frustrations because our baseline stress is already so high it doesn't take much to tip us over.
sentences.zh: 安静的生活往往恰恰相反，它表明了更强的自我调节能力，因为其中

sentences.en: A quieter life often reflects the opposite and it indicates stronger self-regulation skills because there is
sentences.zh: 进行了一些情感筛选。

sentences.en: some emotional curation going on.
sentences.zh: 你不会对所有事都说好，不会到处都答应去，尤其是当你现在知道了代价之后。

sentences.en: You're not just saying yes to everything, you're not saying yes to being everywhere, especially when you now know the coSt.
sentences.zh: 心理学家有时将其描述为拥有更大的容忍窗口。

sentences.en: Psychologists sometimes describe this as having a greater window of tolerance.
sentences.zh: 基本上，你能更好地围绕自己能容忍的事情做出决定，并且能够更好地扩展自己应对突发状况的能力，因为

sentences.en: Basically, you're better able to make decisions around what you can tolerate and you're better able to expand your capacity to deal with things coming out of the blue because
sentences.zh: 你没有不断地用那些其实根本无需忍受的事情来加重你的情绪系统负担。

sentences.en: you're not constantly taxing your emotional systems with stuff you actually don't need to endure.
sentences.zh: 还有关于一种叫做享乐适应的研究。

sentences.en: There's also research around something called hedonic adaptation.
sentences.zh: 你以前可能在播客里听过这个，但关于纯粹的新鲜感、纯粹的混乱和纯粹的刺激，最关键的是我们的大脑会对此习以为常，所以你

sentences.en: You've probably heard about this on the podcast before, but the thing about raw novelty and raw chaos and raw excitement is that our brain gets really used to it and so you
sentences.zh: 需要越来越多的刺激才能感到快乐。

sentences.en: need more and more and more to enjoy yourself.
sentences.zh: 你的神经系统会重新校准，因此当你习惯了这些巨大刺激时，小小的快乐就会变得不再那么快乐。

sentences.en: Your nervous system recalibrates and so it makes it so that small pleasures don't feel as pleasurable anymore when you're used to this big stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以回归这种平静、较慢的生活能让你真正地向相反方向重新校准。

sentences.en: So going back to this peaceful slower life allows you to actually recalibrate it back in the opposite direction.
sentences.zh: 你能够真正对那些你可以而且应该心存感激的事物产生更多的感激之情。

sentences.en: You're able to actually have more of an appreciation for just things that you can and should be grateful for.
sentences.zh: 其次，不言而喻的是，更平淡的生活往往也意味着拥有更好的界限，因为在那时，最重要的是你的情感和

sentences.en: Secondly, it goes without saying, but a more boring life is also often a life with better boundaries because at that point what matters most is your emotional and your
sentences.zh: 心理中心，而不是别人对你的偏好，也不是你没有出现是否会让人失望。

sentences.en: psychological centre, not someone else's preferences for you, not whether you disappointed somebody by not showing up.
sentences.zh: 你能很快看清究竟是谁因为你是你而喜欢你，又是谁喜欢你能提供给他们什么。

sentences.en: You get pretty clear on who likes you for you compared with who likes what you can offer them fairly quickly.
sentences.zh: 当然，伴随着更好的界限，也会带来更大的当下的觉知。

sentences.zh: 就像哲学家们一直在谈论的当下一样，当然，伴随着更好的界限，它也带来了更大的当下觉知。

sentences.en: What philosophers like people have been talking about presence for ages and of course alongside better boundaries it also comes with greater presence.
sentences.zh: 就像哲学家们字面意义上几百年来所说的那样，这是生活最珍贵的礼物，因为没有它，其他一切都不可能实现。

sentences.en: What philosophers like literally hundreds of years have said is like life's most precious gift because nothing else is possible without it.
sentences.zh: 就像那是你没有意识到的。

sentences.en: You're not really present for those moments of chaos and like glamour and excitement.
sentences.zh: 有数千篇古代文献、数千本书籍、数千篇文章都在探讨如何真正充分利用每一个时刻。

sentences.en: There are thousands of ancient texts, thousands of books, thousands of articles that have been written about how to really take everything from a moment.
sentences.zh: 如何调整你的感官和心智去欣赏大多数人忽略的细节。

sentences.en: How to attune your senses and your mind to appreciate details that most of us ignore.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，他们建议的重要部分往往是：花更多时间去体验无聊，花更多时间融入平凡。

sentences.en: And no surprise here a big part of their advice is often spend more time being bored, spend more time within the ordinary.
sentences.zh: 翻译一下，就是说慢他妈的下来哪怕一会儿。

sentences.en: Translation like just like slow the fuck down for just a second.

sentences.zh: 你有没有回想过某次非常棒的假期、非常棒的夜生活或者非常棒的生日，然后意识到，其实我根本不记得我以为自己会记住的事情。

sentences.en: I remember the strangest little details.
